sara: Heads-up — ran the new quantized-embed runner on the MTEB-like rerank suite and local vs CI NDCG drift is reproducible. Local single-process run: ndcg@10=0.512, CI aggregated run: ndcg@10=0.498. Only for int8 PQ embeddings and when we enable shard merging.

liam: do you have a minimal repro? sounds like a merge/tie-break ordering issue between shards. :thinking_face:

sara: yes, repro is trivial. run this:
```
python eval_runner.py --suite rerank_mteb --model my-quantized-int8 --topk 100 --seed 42 --shards 4 --merge-strategy heap
```
Local vs CI: run the same command on CI (we shard into 4) and then compare ndcg after merge. attaching a tiny log snippet:
```
[run] shard-0 topk scores: [0.912, 0.897, 0.897, 0.871]
[run] shard-1 topk scores: [0.912, 0.897, 0.897, 0.870]
[merge] merged topk (CI): [0.912, 0.897, 0.897, 0.897, ...]
[local] merged topk (single proc): [0.912, 0.897, 0.897, 0.871, ...]
```
Notice different order for items with equal-ish scores (quantization causes many ties).
```
# quick check: stable compare
candidates.sort(key=lambda c: (-c.score, c.doc_id))
```

james: that matches what I saw when we switched the default merge to heapq.nlargest — heapq is not stable across equal keys and Python's float rounding with fp16/int8 can flip bit patterns. We should make the merge deterministic by adding a deterministic tie-breaker (doc id) and avoid relying on heap ordering.

eve: more detail: our per-shard topk is correct, but the merge step currently does: `global_topk = heapq.nlargest(K, itertools.chain(*shard_iters), key=lambda c: c.score)` then we compute ranks. Because heapq uses comparison only on the key, the relative order of equal keys depends on insertion order across iterators which varies by concurrency in CI. When scores tie, ndcg can jump depending on which doc lands earlier at cutoff.

liam: proposed patch: change merge to collect candidate tuples and use a stable sort: `global_topk = sorted(itertools.chain(*shard_iters), key=lambda c: (-c.score, c.doc_id))[:K]` This is O(N log N) but N is small (sum topk across shards). We can micro-opt: use a stable partial sort that keeps doc_id tie-breaker. Also add a deterministic seed param to shard iteration order.

james: also add a unit test that constructs artificial equal-score candidates and asserts deterministic ordering across many shuffle permutations. Something like:
```
def test_merge_stability():
    shards = [list(shuffle_with_seed(base_candidates, s)) for s in range(10)]
    orders = [merge_shards(sh) for sh in shards]
    assert all(o == orders[0] for o in orders)
```

sara: re: CI wiring — the flaky test surfaced because our CI splits the suite into dynamic job chunks and then aggregates metrics by concatenating per-job outputs and feeding to the metric calculator without normalizing rank ties. We should ensure the metric calculator is fed the final deterministic ranking (post-merge). Right now some jobs write per-shard intermediate JSON and the aggregator simply concatenates them.

eve: in the aggregator code there's a subtle bug: when `aggregate_runs()` merges JSONL from jobs it does `global_candidates.extend(shard['candidates'])` without rescoring or re-sorting. So the metric module computes ranks on the concatenated list order rather than doing an explicit sort. Fix is to call `compute_final_ranking(global_candidates)` which sorts with the stable tie-breaker before metrics.

ci-bot: CI job 4521 re-run queued by @sara — https://ci.redwood.ai/job/4521

liam: I pushed a draft PR with both fixes and the new unit test: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-runner/pull/1245 — it uses stable sort and adds a `MERGE_TIEBREAK` env var.

james: nice. can you also emit a warning when we see many exact-equal scores (threshold of identical bits) so ops know quantization is introducing ties? maybe metric.alerts can track %equal_topk.

sara: good call. created INF ticket INF-7890 and pinned the failing CI run + dashboard: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-7890 
and dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/ndcg-regressions?run=1850001111

eve: test plan: 1) land PR 1245, 2) run full rerank suite (quantized + fp16) in CI with `MERGE_TIEBREAK=docid`, 3) verify ndcg variance across 5 CI repeats < 0.001, 4) add alert if >1% topk are exact-ties.

sara: assigning to @liam for patch follow-up and @james for CI wiring. will monitor dashboard. thanks everyone :tada:
